gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-mayan-nu: Contemporary and a bit unusual, Origami draws its lowercase like poured lead in a single brushed line, over Noto Sans Mayan Numerals with tall bodies and a gaping c. A slightly larger body size would help.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-medefaid: Contemporary through and through, Origami cuts every letter at a single depth like an engraver's tool, with no deeper spots. gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-meetei-m: Brushed and blocky, Origami has no hairlines anywhere in its alphabet, while Noto Sans Meetei Mayek has rounds that gap like a cracked bangle. Give the body a little extra size.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-mende-ki: Noto Sans Mende Kikakui lets daylight through every curved opening and stands its lowercase tall against the capitals. And Origami, with no thick-thin swell a pointed brush would give, makes a good foil; nudging the body size up helps those openings.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-meroitic: Origami looks like stitched thread outlines, plain strokes in a lowercase mass heavy as poured lead type. And Noto Sans Meroitic fills each line with see-through c shapes and capital-sized lowercase, so long text feels friendly and approachable.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-modi: Noto Sans Modi lets daylight into every curve and keeps its capitals and lowercase close in height. Origami, a single-weight outline feel in sign-painter's brush, gives way to that body so a long passage reads smooth and modern.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-mono: Origami has a marker-drawn plainness in every character, and it earns its keep big and short. Noto Sans Mono follows with generously spaced letters and tall lowercase that make words look sturdy.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-mro: Zero stroke contrast anywhere makes Origami look like a sign-painter's brush moving at constant width. gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-multani: Noto Sans Multani reads modern, with a lofty x-height and a wide gap at the e's terminal. Origami's constant-width, sign-painter brush look sets it apart, and that single-stroke sturdiness against the open body is the pair's strongest quality.
